title: Teaching: ultrasound-guided IJV central line
stem: Teaching room. Your junior needs to learn how to insert an ultrasound-guided right internal jugular central line for a ventilated patient in septic shock on noradrenaline. Teach the procedure on the manikin.

phases.title: Demonstrate
phases.goal: Time-out, then the whole line on the manikin, each safety check as you do it.

notes:
Checked against NICE TA49 (ultrasound guidance for central venous access), the Association of Anaesthetists 2016 safe vascular access guideline, and the NHS 'Safety Standards for Invasive Procedures' (NatSSIPs 2023).

Indications: vasopressors, poor peripheral access, CVP/ScvO2, irritant drugs. Relative contraindications: overlying infection, thrombosis, coagulopathy (weigh up), contralateral pneumothorax. Steps: consent (or best interests), NatSSIPs checklist and time-out, full barrier precautions (cap, mask, sterile gown and gloves, full-length drape), 2% chlorhexidine in 70% alcohol allowed to dry, head-down tilt, real-time ultrasound (identify the IJV lateral to the carotid, compressible, non-pulsatile; confirm needle tip in the vein), Seldinger technique (needle, wire never let go, confirm the wire in the vein on ultrasound, nick, dilate, catheter to about 15 cm on the right), aspirate and flush every lumen, secure, dressing, chest X-ray (tip at the cavo-atrial junction, no pneumothorax), document, and count the wire out. Complications: arterial puncture/cannulation (do not dilate an artery — leave the catheter and call vascular), pneumothorax, air embolism (head down, occlude hubs), arrhythmia (withdraw wire), lost guidewire, infection, thrombosis.

Your notes (checklist, ultrasound, Seldinger mnemonic, complications, depth 15–16 cm right) match this.

The demonstration is a hands-on bench (perform: cvc), checked step by step against the MSD Manual internal jugular cannulation steps (Trendelenburg 15–20°, slight head turn, pre-flushed lumens, J-wire 10–15 cm on the right and back off with ectopics, never lose grasp of the wire, #11 stab of about 4 mm, twisting dilator, wire out of the hub before the catheter enters, at least 15 cm on the right, aspirate and flush, X-ray before use) and the short-axis dynamic needle tip positioning technique (45–60°, slide the probe until the tip disappears, advance until it reappears; wire seen in the vein before dilating). Head rotation: more turn increases carotid overlap in many patients (Sulek 1996), so only a slight turn.

Perfect script checked against NICE TA49 and NatSSIPs, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme.

script.say: Great start. By the end you'll know each step and the safety checks, and practise on the manikin. What worries you most?

He is ventilated and cannot consent, so this is a best-interests decision, recorded. Before we scrub, the NatSSIPs checklist and time-out: right patient, right IJ, platelets and INR fine, ultrasound here, full kit, wire count one.

script.do: On the manikin: bed 15° head-down, head turned slightly left. Pre-scan at the cricoid: vein centred, lateral to the carotid, compressible under the probe. Full barrier precautions: cap and mask, scrub, gown, gloves. Chlorhexidine 2% in alcohol 30 s, left to dry; full-length drape. Lumens flushed, blue and white clamped, brown open; probe in a sterile sheath.
Lidocaine wheal. Needle at 45° under real-time ultrasound, aspirating: slide the probe on, advance to the dot, again, until the front wall tents and dark blood fills the syringe.
Steady the needle, syringe off, thumb on the hub. J-wire to 15–20 cm, never letting go; back off if ectopics. Pinch the wire at the skin; needle off. Wire seen in the vein in short and long axis.

4 mm stab at the wire, edge away. Dilate: down the wire, take the tail, twist in to the vein only, out, gauze. Catheter down the wire, wire out of the brown hub and held, catheter to 15 cm. Wire out, shown whole: count it out.
Aspirate and flush every lumen, cap them. Stitch both wings; chlorhexidine dressing. X-ray: tip at the cavo-atrial junction, no pneumothorax. Document the wire count.

script.do: Leave the catheter in, don't pull it, and call vascular. Then you'd confirm with a gas or a transduced trace.
